## Active

### D-029 — blong-int-adapter tests leave redis keys that break the commander

> _2026-08-23 · test/blong-int-adapter · active_

Running the `blong-int-adapter` redis tests seeds `blong-test:*` keys into redis database 0, and the
commander's explore tree renders every key (only its table is filtered), so its Playwright baseline
changes; the gateway meter tests add `{app:*}` keys the same way. Both families are disposable test
artifacts: clean database 0 and re-seed `commander:demo`/`commander:greeting` before and after
running them. One local run needed 29 leftover keys removed with a Lua `DEL` loop that leaves all
other keys untouched; `redis-cli` is not installed on this host, so use ioredis from
`core/blong-gogo`.

### D-057 — Integration tests cover resource-backed CRUD and graph edges

> _2026-08-19 · test/blong-int-adapter · active_

`@feasibleone/blong-core` was wired as a mysql realm child (user-approved) and a
`mysql resource/edge CRUD` group was added with 12 steps: resource-backed person CRUD, ulid/uuid PK
generation, a `hasMember` graph-edge team master-detail, and cascade remove. All pass. Noted:
binary(16) columns round-trip as 24-character base64, not as a 26-character ULID, which is
documented in the blong-schema skill.

### D-995 — The performance thresholds live in a support file and the test reads them

> _2026-11-24 · test/blong-int-adapter · active_

A number asserted in a test and explained nowhere is a number somebody loosens. The measurement
method, the topic shape and the accepted throughput and p95 are written in `kafka-perf.md` beside
this package; the test asserts them and prints the measured values, and every run writes a report
with the distribution and a chart.

### D-1039 — Integration files run under a wider tap budget

> _2026-11-28 · test/blong-int-adapter · active_

The integration harness now runs with a 180 second tap budget, set from `tapConfig.ts` — a module
`test.ts` imports before `tap` — rather than from a flag in a package script. The default was spent
on the load alone: a file starts a process against real backends (~8 s), and the kafka file then
runs its perf scenarios (a burst pattern with seconds of deliberate silence), which together left a
step expiring at ~28 s with the failure reading as a hang in whichever step happened to be running
(`@@F-851`). Two mechanisms are worth knowing: `tap.test(name, {timeout: …})` did not raise the
budget of the steps a run creates, and setting the environment variable at the top of `test.ts` came
too late because tap reads its configuration when it is evaluated — so the setting lives in its own
module, imported first. The budget is per file, so a genuine hang still fails: every step keeps its
own polling deadline, and the one that stalls is named in the report.

### D-1038 — A test instance answers as the realm's own namespace

> _2026-11-28 · test/blong-int-adapter · active_

The admin instance answers as `kafka` — the realm's own subject — rather than as a coined second
word of its own. That word existed for one mechanical reason: `exec` reads only the second and third
parts of a method name, so a namespace of its own pushed every call into four parts — a resolve read
as `topic.resolve` under it needs a handler file whose name is the four words glued together, and
the extra word was all that stood between the name and the operation. Naming the namespace after the
subject keeps every call a clean triple (`kafka.topic.resolve`, `kafka.client.list`,
`kafka.feed.record.handle`), needs nothing added to the dictionary, and makes the port's reach
obvious: everything under `kafka.` belongs to that instance. A second word is worth coining only
when two instances must be told apart from outside — here the round-trip instances answer as
`broker` and `telemetry`, so nothing collided.

The same rule decides the broker's names: every topic and every consumer group this suite uses
starts with `blong-int-adapter`, so a broker shared with the commander, the agent or another
checkout's run carries this suite's records under one prefix an operator can recognise, and a group
names the role it plays (`blong-int-adapter.stream` for the round trip,
`blong-int-adapter.feed.glob` for the feed that reads a pattern). The prefix is stated once, in
`kafka/meta/kafka/*.yaml` for the topics and in the adapters' specs for the groups, and the coverage
matrix in the package README names the topics so a rename is a line a reviewer sees.
